stem: ![](asset:P000165-stem-1)If position-time graph of a particle is a sine curve as shown, then which one will be the corresponding velocity-time graph:

assets.alt: Position x against time t: a wave-shaped curve starting at the origin, dipping below the axis, then rising above it.
Velocity v against time t: starts at a positive maximum, falls through zero to a negative minimum and rises back to the maximum (a cosine-shaped curve starting high).
Velocity v against time t: starts at zero, dips negative, then rises to a positive hump and returns to zero (a sine-shaped curve starting downward).
Velocity v against time t: starts at a negative minimum, rises through zero to a positive maximum and falls back to the negative minimum (a negative-cosine curve).
Velocity v against time t: starts at zero, rises to a positive hump, then dips negative and returns to zero (a sine-shaped curve starting upward).
Two graphs one above the other: position x = −A sin ωt, and velocity v = −Aω cos ωt. A dashed line through the lowest point of x meets v at zero; note: x lowest ⇒ v = 0.
